To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the general education assessment literature provides a rich body of knowledge about the assessment process, including the challenges that institutions and departments face, but it is not a comprehensive resource for understanding the current state of general education assessment; (2) the current state of assessment is characterized by the following: (a) assessment practices are often ad hoc; (b) the majority of institutions do not assess general education outcomes; (c) assessment practices are not well aligned with institutional mission and goals; and

general education assessment practices are changing, that faculty members have a major impact on the success of assessment programs, and that assessment programs are not as successful in meeting the goals of general education reform as is generally assumed.

1) general education assessment practices are changing in the direction of increased attention to the learning of students, increased attention to student learning outcomes, increased attention to the alignment of assessment and instruction, and increased use of multiple methods of assessment; and 2) the most significant change in assessment practices in the last 10 years is the increased attention to student achievement of learning outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model of assessment in higher education, one that is based upon a more comprehensive view of student learning.
the following questions: (1) What are the most important student learning outcomes in the general education curriculum?
the development of assessment practices and tools for use by institutions of higher education in their efforts to improve the general education programs that they offer to their students.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
general education assessment is a complex and challenging process that requires a great deal of time, resources, and effort to be effective.
general education assessment is in its infancy, and the field is just beginning to develop a body of knowledge about what constitutes effective general education assessment.
general education assessment has come far, but still has a long way to go.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a long way to go to develop a coherent set of general education outcomes and assessment practices that will meet the needs of the academy, students, and society.
the general education assessment movement has been a success, and we should build on that momentum.
the assessment of student learning outcomes in the general education curriculum is not a simple matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assessment of general education learning outcomes should be a shared responsibility of all faculty members and that faculty members should have a voice in the design of the assessment process.
general education assessment should be viewed as a complex process that requires multiple measures, including both direct and indirect measures, to be effective.
the general education assessment process is a valuable tool for improving the quality and effectiveness of the curriculum.
